question: Who was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Rammohun Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Raja Rammohun Roy was a prominent social reformer and is known as the father of the Indian Renaissance.
 
• He founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 to fight against social evils like the caste system, child marriage, and Sati.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj played a significant role in the modernization of Indian society and promoted the values of rationalism, humanism, and monotheism.
 
• Raja Rammohun Roy was also instrumental in the abolition of Sati, a practice where widows were forced to self-immolate on their husbands' funeral pyres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj is a socio-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent, founded by Raja Rammohun Roy in 1828.
 
• It aimed to reform and modernize Hindu society by discarding practices like idol worship and promoting monotheism.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj emphasized the importance of reason, morality, and the worship of one God.
 
• It also focused on social reforms such as the abolition of the caste system, women's education, and the fight against child marriage and dowry.
 
 
 
• **Raja Rammohun Roy:**
 
 
• Raja Rammohun Roy (1772-1833) was a prominent Indian social reformer and the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" due to his efforts in bringing about social and educational reforms in India.
 
• Rammohun Roy was a strong advocate for women's rights and played a key role in the abolition of the practice of Sati.
 
• He also promoted the idea of Western education and was instrumental in the establishment of the Hindu College in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms:**
 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was at the forefront of various social reforms in India, advocating for the abolition of practices such as Sati, child marriage, and the caste system.
 
• It promoted women's education and worked towards improving the status of women in society.
 
• The movement also encouraged the adoption of Western education and scientific thinking among Indians.
 
• Through its efforts, the Brahmo Samaj aimed to create a more just and equitable society based on the principles of reason, morality, and monotheism.
